speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing frequent nosebleeds and small red spots on your skin. Can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you have noticed any unusual bruising or bleeding from your gums?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have a history of similar bleeding episodes, and have they suffered any recent viral infections? I also need to know if there is any family history of bleeding disorders or if the child is currently taking any medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to know if the child has had any recent fevers, fatigue, or bone pain, and whether there is any hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy on exam. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and absence of systemic symptoms, this presentation is highly suggestive of a primary hemostasis defect like von Willebrand disease. REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time, Factor_VIII_Activity, vWF_Antigen

speaker: Doctor
text: Since vWF and Factor VIII are normal, I need to assess platelet function more closely. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_aggregation_study

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal platelet count, coagulation factors, and aggregation studies, I suspect a qualitative platelet defect not captured by standard tests, such as Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. REQUEST TEST: Flow_cytometry_for_GPIIb/IIIa

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of GPIIb/IIIa receptors on the platelet surface confirms the diagnosis of Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's thrombasthenia
